import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_77/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_77/training_1.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Operation 1: JOIN on "school_name"
# Both tables have "school_name" column, join on it (inner join by default)
joined_df = pd.merge(df0, df1, on="school_name", how="inner")

# Operation 2: GROUP BY Source5_77_0.school_name, aggregation sum(Source5_77_0.reading_score)
# After join, the reading_score column from Source5_77_0 is "reading_score" (no suffix added because no conflict)
# Group by "school_name" from Source5_77_0 (which is the same as joined "school_name")
grouped_df = joined_df.groupby("school_name", as_index=False)["reading_score"].sum()

# Ensure the schema matches target schema: ['school_name': string, 'reading_score': integer]
# Convert reading_score to integer (sum should be int but just in case)
grouped_df["reading_score"] = grouped_df["reading_score"].astype(int)

# Write the result to the target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_77/target_multisource.csv"
grouped_df.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_77/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_77/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source5_77_0 and Source5_77_1 on school_name (inner join)

# Group by school_name and sum reading_score

# Keep only columns as per target schema
